exclude: RAM a 16 KB C16 does not have
Machine work areas; generated display, 38-by-27 runtime grids and charset; repacker and its earlier copy of $6000-$9FFF
Per-player room-completion flags initialized at $86AE; gap before room records
Retained relocation tail: $C820-$C8FF equals $8820-$88FF; the rest is power-on RAM and machine data, including the copied KERNAL keyboard scanner

comments.text: Selects keyboard, music and one player; copies the KERNAL keyboard code from ROM $DB00-$E4FF into the RAM beneath it, patches that copy at $DB7D, installs game_irq at the hardware vector, and banks out the ROMs. Sets PAL/NTSC timing, multicolour text and the RAM charset, copies 256 glyphs from charset_seed to $5000, then enters the title/game cycle.

Clears the completion flash and calls title_screen, which clears both players' room numbers and may select a demonstration room before returning. On return, clears both players' scores and camera state, resets Santa's direction and the six-frame animation counter, sets player 1's spare-life count to BCD 2, and starts the room loop. The title routine initializes player 2 according to the selected player count.
Loads the active player's room and waits until both camera-direction bytes are zero before entering play. The non-demo path then cycles the room label's colours before enabling the countdown.

Enables the timer, checks collected parts against the room requirement, and calls finish_toy when ready. Runs object sweeps while unpaused, handles room changes, pause, abort and sacrifice input, and branches into the death/next-player sequence when the countdown or a collision ends play.

Scans keyboard row $F7 and tests the mask at $6DB7. A new press toggles paused and timer_running; when pausing, saves sixteen HUD characters and colours and displays GAME PAUSED, then restores the saved cells on resume. The held-key latch at $5F prevents repeated toggles.

Stops the timer and clears voice 1's frequency high bits. Carry set on the RUN/STOP sacrifice path skips directly to the snowball wipe. With carry clear for timeout/collision, a demonstration returns to the title; normal play runs an object-update delay before the wipe and the next-player or high-score decision.

Silences sound, marks the life as ended and fills the 38-by-27 room with tile 4. First plots 4,352 pseudorandom positions using TED timer and horizontal-counter bits, then traverses every coordinate to finish the snowball fill. Delays before the player/high-score decision.
Three bytes copied over the KERNAL keyboard scanner at $DB7D: 4c 9a db. The startup keeps the scanner available from RAM while the ROMs are disabled.
Sixteen ASCII bytes containing GAME PAUSED, padded with spaces; poll_pause adds $4F to letters and uses glyph 0 for spaces.
Sixteen-byte runtime buffer for the HUD characters covered by GAME PAUSED. poll_pause writes it before displaying the message and restores it on resume.
Sixteen-byte runtime buffer paired with pause_saved_chars; preserves the HUD attributes behind the pause message.

Copies the 25-byte source at grid_pointer_helper to RAM $0400, retaining the source bytes as well. On exit Y is $FF and A is $A5, the first copied opcode; STA through the $0409 pointer at index $FF sets the machine's $0508 reset marker to $A5. The simulation calls the helper's copy at $0400.

Resets per-room state and sound, blanks the display, restores the three brick glyphs animated on the title screen and the HUD, and reads the active player's room and completion flag. Copies a 448-byte window beginning at the room's toy-picture pointer into $55A8; for a shorter picture this includes subsequent picture data. Selects required parts and time, expands the packed 38-by-27 map into both grids, draws each tile and records Santa's start, then enables the display and interrupts.

Decodes one 38-cell room row high nibble first. Tile 9 receives its room-specific door information from door_links; tile 6 becomes bonus tile 5 in a completed room. Writes both simulation grids, records tile 10 as Santa's position and plots the tile. Advances grid pointers by 38 until all 27 rows are drawn.
Sixteen bytes for DEMO PRESS A KEY, with ASCII letters and $B1 separators. The demonstration HUD adds $4F to every byte, turning the separators into blank glyph 0.
Reads the active player's packed-BCD spare-life count and draws its tens and units as stacked digit halves in the MEN field. The initial value is 2, in addition to the life being played.
Calls reveal_toy_part repeatedly until parts_collected equals parts_required, preserving X on the stack. Used when entering a room that player's completion flag already marks complete.

Sixteen per-room delay counts, read at $6550 and written into the immediate operand at $6FFC. Values decline from 10 for the first rooms to 1 for the last, reducing the busy-wait inside the simulation sweep.

Scans the first 38-by-27 room grid. Replaces low-nibble tile 6 (toy part) with tile 5 (bonus), preserving bit 7, writes the result to both grids and redraws converted cells. The caller clears current-room flag $42 and caps surplus time at BCD $0040; the persistent per-player flag is written on room exit at $61AA.

Saves A/X/Y and clears decimal mode, acknowledges TED's interrupt and selects title or play work. In play it copies the camera window, handles the completion flash and countdown, moves the camera every other interrupt, updates animated glyphs and the time/lives HUD, and runs the music routine. In title mode it animates three brick glyphs and calls the copied KERNAL keyboard scan. Restores the saved registers and returns with RTI.

Rewrites the source operands in the unrolled screen-copy loop from camera_ptr. Consecutive source rows are 76 bytes apart; copies 24 characters from each of 25 rows of the full room character plane at $1000 into the left 24 columns of the visible $0C00 screen. The 24-row TED window clips its top and bottom.

The single byte $08 between copy_camera_window's RTS and animate_tile_glyphs. It is not an instruction in either routine.

Runs when frame_counter is divisible by four. Advances an eight-frame counter and a six-frame counter, selects animation pointers from $6A97-$6AFA, and copies 32-byte frames into ten live glyph groups, including Santa's direction-dependent group and the tiles reused by the room display.
8 pointers to 32-byte frames for magic grid. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
12 pointers to 32-byte frames for Santa, three groups of four frames selected by santa_direction. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for water. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for ordinary and gift-producing explosions, copied to both live glyph groups. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for polar bear alternate orientation. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for polar bear. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for penguin. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
4 pointers to 32-byte frames for penguin alternate orientation. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.
6 pointers to 32-byte frames for bonus, in descending frame-address order. animate_tile_glyphs reads these addresses for the live charset copies.

If second_divider is nonzero, decrements it and returns. At zero, reloads video_rate and subtracts one from the two-byte BCD countdown. Clears timer_running when both time bytes become zero. The reload is 50 on PAL and 60 on NTSC, so successive subtraction events are rate+1 calls apart.
Converts the three visible decimal digits from the two-byte BCD countdown into pairs of vertically stacked font characters at $0D8D-$0D8F and $0DB5-$0DB7.

On alternate frames, walks the sixteen-byte warning_palette table and applies its colours to the two MEN label/number rows. Repeats the cycle according to $57 and clears the active flag at $55 when the repeat count reaches zero.
Sixteen TED colour/luminance bytes, from dark blue through brighter blue and back, read by the life and low-time flashing routines. The low-time routine indexes the first sixteen entries.

With time's high byte zero and the low BCD byte below $11, initializes and cycles a sixteen-entry colour index and colours the two TIME rows from warning_palette. Does nothing when the remaining time is outside that range.

Counts Santa as present in this sweep, refreshes the grid pointers from the helper copied to $0400, and checks that the current cell still contains Santa. If so, polls and attempts movement and checks neighbouring enemies; otherwise enters kill_santa.

Uses demo steering or the selected physical controls. Tries vertical movement first; if it fails, tries horizontal movement. With no requested direction, resets the Santa animation-direction selector.

Builds a neighbour offset from the selected axis and input sign, accepts empty/snow cells, collects stationary bonus or toy-part tiles, handles horizontal snowball pushing, and enters a door only when the toy is complete and fire is held. Carry reports an accepted move/action; clear carry permits the other axis to be tried.

Preserves the tile code while saving the music registers for an effect. Toy parts call reveal_toy_part and increment parts_collected; reaching parts_required starts a screen flash and a higher-pitched tone. Bonuses use the ordinary collection tone. Starts a voice-2 effect and clears voice 1's enable bit. music_tick restores a pending save only when its input latch is nonzero and both effect_active and life_ended are clear.

Saves the neighbour offset. With fire held, clears and redraws that neighbour while Santa stays put. Otherwise clears Santa's old cell, places tile 10 in the chosen neighbour, updates the world coordinate and player-grid pointer, sets the demo heading and redraws the new cell.

Source of the helper copied to $0400. Copies player_grid_ptr to the second-grid pointer, subtracts $0600 for the first-grid pointer, and copies Santa's world coordinates into the tile drawing coordinates. The player pointer is one row and one column before Santa, making offset $27 its current cell in a 38-column grid.
One zero byte copied with grid_pointer_helper's 24 instruction bytes to $0400. It lies after that helper's RTS.

Uses controls_mode's sign bit to select keyboard or joystick port 2. Returns signed horizontal/vertical intents in $1D/$1E and fire in $1F. The joystick path clears the keyboard row latch before selecting $FD/$FF08; the keyboard path scans P/L, A/S and SPACE through scan_matrix_row.
Eight active-low keyboard column masks: P=$02, C=$10, M=$10, L=$04, A=$04, S=$20, H=$20 and SPACE/ESC=$10. The row selected at each call distinguishes keys sharing a column.

Accepts horizontal neighbours only. The square beyond the ball must be exactly empty in the second grid, and TED's horizontal-position read must be below $60. Moves the ball two cells from Santa, clears its former cell, then enters the ordinary Santa move path. A failed test returns clear carry.
Clears the selected neighbouring cell in the first grid and redraws empty tile 0 through the matching directional store helper. Returns carry set without changing Santa's coordinates.

Refreshes the player-relative grid pointers, saves music registers if no effect is active, sets life_ended, draws the nine-cell death explosion, and starts a voice-2 noise effect at frequency $094 with control $4F.

Traverses a 3-by-3 neighbourhood using explosion_offsets and coordinate deltas. Leaves solid tile 8 and low-nibble door tile 9 in place; writes ordinary explosion tile $0B into the other cells of both simulation grids and redraws them.

Nine offsets into the player-relative grid window: 0,1,2,$26,$27,$28,$4C,$4D,$4E. Followed at $6E94 and $6E9D by the incremental X and Y drawing deltas used to visit those cells from bottom-right toward top-left.

Calls the grid helper at $0400, then examines the four cardinal neighbours of Santa. A neighbour with low-nibble tile 2 or 3 discards this routine's return address and jumps into kill_santa. Other neighbours leave play running.
Player-relative offsets for up, right, down and left: 1,$28,$4D,$26. Used to check Santa's contact with either enemy type.

Gives tile 5 a score increment of 2 and tile 6 an increment of 1 in the internal BCD score, whose displayed trailing zero makes these 20 and 10 points. Saves the previous thousands digit for the extra-life check, adds to the active player's two-byte score and falls through to draw_score.

Draws four packed-BCD score digits as stacked glyph pairs; the HUD's trailing zero supplies the fifth displayed digit. Compares the current thousands digit with the saved one, awards a spare life when it changed, starts the MEN colour flash and redraws the life count. Preserves the caller's Y through scratch $02.
When effect_active is zero, copies the five TED sound registers $FF0E-$FF12 into music_register_save at $851B. Leaves an already active effect's original saved music state intact.

Traverses the interior room cells from top left, reading the first grid and writing the second. Handles falling/rolling snowballs and parcels, dispatches enemies, water, explosions, magic grids and Santa, and checks that Santa was found. Copies four pages of the resulting second grid back to the first after the sweep.

Tests the cell below a snowball, bonus or toy part. Empty space permits a downward move with bit 7 set; Santa below is entered only when the current object was already marked falling. On other supports, tiles 4 through 9 lead to left-first then right rolling tests.

Advances the two grid pointers and tile coordinate, waits the room-specific immediate delay at $6FFC, and steps across the interior rows. At the end, checks Santa's presence and copies $2800-$2BFF back to $2200-$25FF for the next sweep.
Immediate byte in LDX at $6FFB. load_room writes the current room's room_step_delays entry here; the following DEX/BNE loop sets part of the simulation's pacing.

Selects ordinary explosion $0B for enemy type 2 or gift-producing explosion $0E for type 3. Writes a 3-by-3 blast into both grids except solid tile 8 and doors, redraws the cells and starts the voice-2 noise effect. Returns to the simulation's next-cell path.

Checks exact-empty down-left and left cells first, then rejects rolling left when the above-left cell masked with $7F is tile 4, 5 or 6. If blocked, checks exact-empty down-right and right cells, then rejects rolling right when the above-right cell's low nibble is 4, 5 or 6. Clears the current cell and moves the object sideways with bit 7 set for a later fall.

Only spreads when TED horizontal position XOR timer 1's low byte is below $20. Tests left, right, down then up in the second grid and writes water tile $0C into the first neighbour whose low nibble is below 4. Retains the source water cell.

If a snowball/parcel is immediately above, makes an ordinary nine-cell explosion. Otherwise uses bits 4-5 as a heading and tests direction-relative offsets to choose an empty neighbour, clears the source, writes the heading-tagged type-2 tile and draws its oriented glyph group.

A snowball, bonus or parcel directly above, stationary or falling, makes a gift-producing nine-cell explosion: the test masks away bit 7. Otherwise chooses among empty neighbours using the opposite directional preference from type 2, writes a heading-tagged type-3 tile and draws its oriented glyph group.

Four groups of four offsets into the 38-column grid window. The first group is up,left,down,right (1,$26,$4D,$28); the next groups are its rotations. Enemy steering and demonstration steering index these groups by the current heading.

If Santa has not yet been counted in this sweep, preserves the grid pointers and drawing coordinates on the stack, runs update_santa and restores the scanner's state. Continues at next_world_cell, preventing a moved Santa from receiving a second input step.

Uses a tile's high nibble as its animation age. Increments the age until it reaches 3; then ordinary explosion $0B becomes empty, while gift explosion $0E becomes a toy part or a bonus according to room_incomplete. Redraws the changed cell.

Requires an exact stationary snowball tile 4 directly above and an empty cell directly below. Removes the snowball above and creates a falling toy part ($86), or falling bonus ($85) in a completed room, below. Leaves the magic-grid cell in place.
Stores A into offset $27 of the second grid, the scanner's current cell, then draws it through draw_tile.
Stores A into second-grid offset 1, temporarily decrements tile_y and draws the tile, then restores tile_y.
Stores A into second-grid offset $26, temporarily decrements tile_x and draws the tile, then restores tile_x.
Stores A into second-grid offset $4D, temporarily increments tile_y and draws the tile, then restores tile_y.
Stores A into second-grid offset $28, temporarily increments tile_x and draws the tile, then restores tile_x.

Masks A to its low-nibble tile kind, looks up the 76-character-wide plane row at tile_rows, and adds twice tile_x. Writes four consecutive glyph codes from tile_glyphs as a two-by-two character block. Disables interrupts for the four stores and enables them afterward.
Thirty pointers, $1000 + row*152, into the full-room character plane. draw_tile indexes by twice tile_y; the stored room has 27 rows, with three additional row pointers retained in this table.
Writes the heading-tagged enemy into second-grid offset 1, draws it with draw_enemy while tile_y is temporarily one less, then restores the coordinate.
Writes the enemy into second-grid offset $26 and draws its oriented shape one tile left of the current coordinates.
Writes the enemy into second-grid offset $4D and draws its oriented shape one tile below the current coordinates.
Writes the enemy into second-grid offset $28 and draws its oriented shape one tile right of the current coordinates.

Computes the same two-by-two destination as draw_tile. Selects a heading-specific base glyph from enemy2_glyphs or enemy3_glyphs using scratch $02, and writes the four consecutive glyph codes with interrupts temporarily disabled.

Uses room*16 + parts_collected to select a toy-cell position from toy_positions and a graphic-piece number from toy_pieces. Looks up the visible two-by-two cell pointer and writes four glyph codes starting at $B5 + piece*4. Preserves Y on the stack.
Fifteen pointers into the five-column by three-row toy diagram at the HUD's lower right. reveal_toy_part indexes this table with toy_positions.
Seventeen base-glyph codes in steps of four from $00 to $40. draw_tile indexes by the masked low nibble, so its 0-15 tile kinds use the first sixteen entries; the retained seventeenth value is $40.
Four direction-dependent base glyphs for enemy type 2: $3C,$3C,$08,$08. draw_enemy adds 0,1,2,3 for the tile's four character cells.
Four direction-dependent base glyphs for enemy type 3: $0C,$40,$40,$0C, used for the penguin's two orientations.
Sixteen packed-map pointers from $A800 to $C61E, spaced by $0202. load_room reads 513 bytes high nibble first for each room's 38*27 tiles; each 514-byte allocation retains one extra byte.
Sixteen blue luminance values used for the room-label colour cycle when entering play: $76 down to $06 and back upward. The loop indexes the cycle repeatedly before enabling the timer.

Startup charset source, glyphs $00-$1F: the first four cells for each tile kind from empty through brick. game_entry copies eight 256-byte pages from this source into the 256-glyph live charset at $5000.
Startup glyphs $20-$3F: wall, door, Santa, explosions, water, magic grid and an enemy orientation. Animated groups are replaced during the game.
Startup glyphs $40-$5F, including the alternate penguin and title decorations; the page is copied to live glyphs $40-$5F at $5200.
Startup glyphs $60-$7F: title/font shapes and the beginning of the stacked numeric glyphs, copied to $5300.
Startup glyphs $80-$9F: numeric halves and alphabet characters. ASCII letters are displayed at their byte value plus $4F.
Startup glyphs $A0-$B4 contain Q-Z, the single-height digits 0-9 and the name-entry cursor. The blank used by string printing is glyph $00. Glyphs $B5 onward are populated from animation/toy data.
Eight 32-byte two-by-two-character animation frames for magic-grid tile 13, selected through magic_animation_ptrs.
Twelve 32-byte frames for Santa: three direction groups of four frames, selected through santa_animation_ptrs.
Four 32-byte frames for water, copied into the live $30-$33 glyphs.
Four 32-byte explosion frames. animate_tile_glyphs uses the same frame in the ordinary and gift-explosion live glyph groups.
Four 32-byte polar-bear frames for the alternate orientation at live glyphs $3C-$3F.
Four 32-byte polar-bear frames at live glyphs $08-$0B.
Four 32-byte penguin frames at live glyphs $0C-$0F.
Four 32-byte penguin frames for the alternate orientation at live glyphs $40-$43.
The first two of six consecutive 32-byte bonus frames; the other four begin at bonus_frames_high. bonus_animation_ptrs reads the six in descending address order.
The other four 32-byte bonus frames from the six-frame block beginning at $7FC0. Separated here because $8000 is a memory-map boundary.

Fifteen rows of sixteen character codes, copied to the right-hand HUD by load_room. Contains the ICICLE WORKS title, PLAYER/ROOM, TIME/SCORE/MEN labels and their initial digits. The title screen borrows the logo rows.

Runs while input_latch is nonzero. Restarts the selected tune when both channels have ended, defers music while an effect or life end is active, and restores the saved TED sound registers after an effect. Advances a channel when its duration counter is zero and decays the shared volume toward 2 on a two-call envelope cycle.

X selects voice 0 or 1. Reads the next low/high pair from that voice's pitch stream, changes TED's frequency and enable bits, and takes its duration from a separate stream. A zero duration ends the channel; a nonzero duration advances its stream, sets volume 8 and restarts the volume envelope.
Uses title_mode (0 for play, 8 for title/high scores) as an offset into music_streams. Loads both voices' pitch and duration pointers, clears their counters and marks both channels active.

Voice-enable masks $10/$20, disable masks $EF/$DF and high-frequency-register indices $12/$10, The register-index pair is $8290/$8291; next_music_note uses it to preserve unrelated bits in $FF12/$FF10.
Two eight-byte tune descriptors. Each contains voice 1 pitch/duration pointers and voice 2 pitch/duration pointers; title_mode selects descriptor offset 0 or 8.

76 little-endian TED frequency words for game music voice 1, including the terminal word read with duration zero. A zero frequency disables the voice; the separate duration stream controls note length.
75 note durations in interrupt calls followed by zero, which ends game music voice 1. The pitch pointer advances by two bytes per duration.

135 little-endian TED frequency words for game music voice 2, including the terminal word read with duration zero. A zero frequency disables the voice; the separate duration stream controls note length.
134 note durations in interrupt calls followed by zero, which ends game music voice 2. The pitch pointer advances by two bytes per duration.

Five-byte runtime save area for TED $FF0E-$FF12, initially zero in the hand-over. Collection and explosion effects save music here. When the music/input latch is nonzero, music_tick restores a pending save after both effect_active and life_ended become clear.

55 little-endian TED frequency words for title music voice 1, including the terminal word read with duration zero. A zero frequency disables the voice; the separate duration stream controls note length.
54 note durations in interrupt calls followed by zero, which ends title music voice 1. The pitch pointer advances by two bytes per duration.

67 little-endian TED frequency words for title music voice 2, including the terminal word read with duration zero. A zero frequency disables the voice; the separate duration stream controls note length.
66 note durations in interrupt calls followed by zero, which ends title music voice 2. The pitch pointer advances by two bytes per duration.

Initializes title/music state, both players' room indices and thirty-two incomplete-room flags. Selects the player-2 life sentinel for one-player mode, blanks and clears the screen, draws the brick frame, icicles, title and option text, then enters title_input_loop.

Draws a two-by-two block of character $1C and colour $79 at the screen pointer, repeats the block count in scratch $04, and advances the pointer by the byte stride in scratch $06. Used for the title frame's horizontal and vertical edges.
Sets up four eighteen-block horizontal bands, alternately using glyph groups $44-$47 and $48-$4B, and draws them with draw_icicle_blocks. Continues into the title logo and text drawing code.

Copies four consecutive character codes starting at scratch $06 into a two-by-two block with colour $71. Advances two screen columns and repeats scratch $04 times, leaving the top-left screen pointer after the strip.

Copies the ICICLE WORKS character rows from the HUD template, gives them colour $71, prints the credit, copyright, option headings and SPACE TO PLAY text, and draws the decorative four-character strip from $8AD1.

Copies a zero-terminated string from scratch pointer $02 into screen pointer $04 and the attribute plane 1 KB below it. Translates an ASCII letter by adding $4F; translates a space through $B1 so that the result wraps to blank glyph 0. Uses scratch $08 as the colour.

Restarts the music streams, refreshes the three option labels, enables the display and interrupts, and waits for SPACE or joystick fire. Polls C/M/P with per-key held latches; each option change resets the idle counter. When the three-byte idle counter expires, sets demo_mode and chooses a room using TED timer bits. The preceding title setup silences sound at $86A7.

Disables interrupts, writes A as the keyboard row/joystick select value to $FD30 and $FF08, reads the active-low latch into A, enables interrupts and returns. The routine enables interrupts regardless of their state on entry.
Selects KEYBOARD or JOYSTICK from controls_mode's sign bit, and sends that text to the title option copier at screen $0EAC.
Selects ON or OFF from music_enabled and sends that text to the title option copier at screen $0EBB.
Selects ONE or TWO from player_count and sends that text to the title option copier at screen $0EC7.
Copies a zero-terminated option string from scratch pointer $04 to screen pointer $02, translating each byte by adding $4F. Does not alter attributes; those are set by title drawing.
Zero-terminated display text: 'BY DOUG TURNER'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'COPYRIGHT COMMODORE'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'CONTROLS      MUSIC      PLAYERS'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'KEYBOARD       ON          ONE'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'SPACE TO PLAY'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Four pre-encoded decorative glyphs copied to title screen $0D84-$0D87, with attribute $71.
Zero-terminated display text: 'KEYBOARD'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'JOYSTICK'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated music option: ON followed by byte $B1. copy_option_text adds $4F to each byte, yielding the O and N glyphs and blank glyph $00.
Zero-terminated display text: 'OFF'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'ONE'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'TWO'. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.

Draws the framed top-ten screen, starts the title tune and checks each player's score for insertion. Displays a continuation prompt and waits for a fresh SPACE/fire press after any name entry. Uses the title interrupt path, including the copied KERNAL keyboard scanner.

Draws ten rows from high_score_records, each 13 bytes apart. Copies each row's rank, name and encoded score into the text screen, sets name/score colours, and appends the final zero glyph of the displayed score.

Ten 13-byte high-score records: two rank columns, a blank, five name glyphs, a blank and four encoded score digits. Ranks 1-9 have a leading blank; rank 10 uses both columns. draw_high_scores appends the displayed trailing zero. Initial names and scores are authored data; insert_high_score shifts and overwrites the records in RAM.
Zero-terminated display text: '    TOP TEN SCORES    '. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: '       SPACE TO CONTINUE      '. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.
Zero-terminated display text: 'PLAYER   ENTER NAME        '. Rendering adds $4F to letters; spaces are mapped to blank glyph 0.

A selects player 0 or 1; doubles it to index the two-byte BCD score pair. Compares against ten scores decoded from stored digit glyphs and accepts a tie. For a qualifying score, reads up to five uppercase letters/spaces from the KERNAL buffer, with DELETE editing and RETURN confirmation, shifts lower entries and stores the new name and score before redrawing the table.

Clears fire and input direction, then follows empty/snow cells using the current heading at $86 and rotated heading_offsets. Turns according to the neighbour tests and converts its chosen heading through demo_dx/demo_dy. It does not use physical controls for movement.
Four signed horizontal intents for headings 0-3: 1,0,-1,0. steer_demo selects the entry for its chosen heading.
Four signed vertical intents paired with demo_dx: 0,-1,0,1. The demonstration starts with a room selected from TED timer bits.
Sixteen required toy-part counts, one per room, read by load_room. They also bound reveal_toy_part and the completed-toy redraw; the unused slots in the per-room order tables remain stored.

Four destination-room numbers per room, assigned to tile-9 cells in row-major order while unpacking. Each destination is stored in that door cell's high nibble; try_santa_move reads it after the room is complete and fire is held.
Sixteen slots per room mapping collection order to one of fifteen visible toy positions. The first room_part_counts[room] entries are consumed; each index selects a pointer in toy_screen_cells.

Sixteen slots per room mapping collection order to 32-byte graphic-piece indices within that room's copied toy graphics. Only the room's required-part count is consumed; retained trailing slots are not treated as additional required pieces.

Sixteen pairs of BCD bytes in high-byte/low-byte order, loaded for an incomplete room in normal play. Completed rooms and demonstrations instead receive $0040 from the code. These stored times are 0120,0080,0090,0095,0065,0050,0055,0060,0090,0085,0070,0060,0070,0065,0055,0055.
